source.title: Efficient Auto-Interpretability of AI Models in Biology

page_placements.theme: SAE latent monosemanticity depends on activation range, scoring metric and evaluation harness

record.tranche_reason: The study measures coherence and descriptions of protein-model SAE latents, not polysemanticity of individual neurons or whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs. Its results concern a related interpretability construct, not one of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports intruder-detection and annotation-validation results for SAE latents. These are adjacent to neuron polysemanticity but do not test whether individual neurons have unrelated meanings, whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition, or whether its prevalence changes as the claim versions describe. Related measurement results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates SAE latents (not individual neurons) of the Boltz-1 protein-structure model for coherence, cross-seed stability and description validity. It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, what causes polysemanticity, or how its prevalence varies. It neither tests nor relies on the claim, so none of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Additions: the authors report that stability prioritisation finds interpretable latents with about 4.4× fewer evaluations and 5.2× lower cost at about 53% recall. Surfaced motifs are significantly enriched for their claimed annotations; residue claims held for all 17, and context claims held for 12 of 16. They recommend ranking rather than excluding by stability and advocate falsifiable ground-truth checks of descriptions.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses cross-seed matching and LLM intruder detection on protein-model SAE latents, rather than investigating individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Intruder-detection scores depend strongly on the output-token allowance and parser; the restricted 16-token gate performs differently across judge models. Calibrated prompt variants score 0.957–0.967, while an independently written paraphrase scores 0.85.

fits_no_version.finding: Intruder-detection scores for protein-model SAE latents collapse to near chance under a 16-token output cap on some judges and recover to about 0.97 at 512 tokens. Prompt wording moves scores from 0.85 to 0.97.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured interpretability of SAE latents by LLM intruder detection depends strongly on the evaluation harness (output-token budget, parser).

fits_no_version.finding: Calibrated intruder accuracy is 0.97 for amino-acid controls, 0.48 for contextual concepts, 0.29 for random latents and 0.17 for the scrambled control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Protein-model SAE latents show a graded range of coherence; most random latents are not judged coherent.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-seed stability predicts SAE latent interpretability, with ρ=0.51 against concept F1 and a 4.4× precision lift. Functional motif latents are less stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents that reproduce across training seeds are more often interpretable, but stability under-selects functional features.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says “Code available here” but gives no URL)
record.problems: Results concern SAE latents rather than individual neurons. The deployment sweep is limited to one model layer and a small panel; the authors also note that the sample of functional motifs is small. Intruder-task calibration showed a substantial harness artifact under the restricted token budget.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly bearing on a listed claim version were extracted. The paper's other stability, cost, and annotation-validation results concern SAE selection and description validation, not neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Neurons in vision classifiers responding to unrelated images.
Share of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer language models and its variation by layer.
Superposition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Effect of activation function, architecture or regularization on the polysemantic share, and the performance cost of lowering it.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons resolve into one shared feature.

Dependence of a neuron's polysemantic classification on the activation range examined or on explanation scoring. The study samples windows across activation deciles but does not report per-decile results bearing on this.

record.verdict_notes: The study concerns SAE latents in a protein-structure model. It contains no neuron-level polysemanticity measurement and no superposition analysis. Rows r2 and r8 report Sonnet 4.6 at 0.97 and 0.96, from different passages.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and individual neurons responding to unrelated image inputs.
MLP neurons in transformer language models and unrelated tokens or contexts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise despite sufficient capacity.
Changes in polysemantic-neuron prevalence across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and performance costs.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons resolve into one shared feature or related jobs with better tools.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on the activation range examined or on how polysemantic explanations are scored.

relation.reason: Acceptable. The text never names polysemanticity, but it does show that auto-interp scores depend on the scoring harness, which sits near V7. No version is tested.

tranche.reason: The study scores the interpretability of Boltz-1 SAE latents (cross-seed stability, intruder detection, description validation). It never measures whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs, and it never mentions polysemanticity or superposition.

source_check.notes: All nine rows are harness-calibration controls on 20 amino-acid SAE latents, not neurons, so none bears on a claim version. The text gives Sonnet 4.6 both 0.97 (Section 2; the inline-CoT bar in Fig. 4) and 0.96 (model comparison), so r2 and r8 probably differ by prompt variant.

statements.correction: 16 tokens: Sonnet 4.6 0.17, Haiku 4.5 0.13, Opus 4.8 0.86 (chance 0.20). 512 tokens: 0.97 headline (Sonnet judge); per model Sonnet 0.96, Haiku 0.97, Opus 0.97, all 20/20. Four phrasings: 0.85-0.97.
statements.problem: No error. All scores are on 20 amino-acid-identity positive-control latents, and the text blames the collapse on the harness (token cap plus fragile parser), not on the latents.
